Slytherin as the misunderstood house: Do you agree/disagree?

I've always been fascinated by what fans have concluded about Slytherin (it's misunderstood, not all who are cunning are evil, etc. etc.), and what J.K. Rowling herself has concluded about Slytherin (i.e. house of evil).

For all the multidimensionality that Rowling brings to her novels, this is the one aspect that irks me the most. Why does all of Slytherin house refuse to help the fight against Voldemort? Why are they all (except Snape) portrayed as evil, hissing, one dimensional caricatures? I feel like J.K. Rowling did a great job of giving other characters in other houses many different personalities, but, with the exception of Snape, kind of dropped the ball with Slytherin.

I think we're more misrepresented than misunderstood. J.K. Rowling is completely biased in her portrayal of Slytherin, but besides that, the only real window into the house is during the years right after Tom Riddle's wrecking of the house's reputation. If a Slytherin had been Headmaster when Tom was a child, he probably wouldn't have been admitted and countless wizard lives would have been saved. And let's just suppose Hermione never got into Hogwarts either. Would her life have been that much worse off? She still would have excelled at school and would have likely gone to Cambridge or Oxford, and likely won a Nobel Prize, furthering scientific knowledge, improving the world for all mankind. Hell, she might have gone on to discover and study magic from a scientific perspective. Her life and talents certainly wouldn't have gone to waste.
